facts.description: Up to 6 checkable facts the coin itself states or visibly rests on, taken from the evidence, the story's before the coin's: first the fact that decides the answer (a likely-false story fact, if any), then the most load-bearing. Empty when the evidence states none.

fact.description: 80 characters at most: one specific, checkable statement the coin makes or rests on, in short plain words that true or false answers.

quote.description: 120 characters at most: the evidence words the fact rests on, copied exactly from the input. A coin fact quotes the coin's own words. A fact with no such words is left out.

source_in_evidence.description: Where the coin says it: its X post or the post that quotes or is quoted, an X Article, its website, its token description, or elsewhere.

about.description: story: the news, event or people the coin rests on (did it happen, is the person who they say). coin: what the coin's own words claim about the coin (that someone made, backs or holds it, or a promise such as "X will claim the fees"). Whether the coin is tied to the story goes in story_link, never here.

opinion.description: likely_true when an independent source checked or witnessed it, or an organisation's or person's own official post or site states its own plain fact (a name, a date, a release, an event it held); likely_false when sources contradict it; self_claimed when the only support is the subject's own word for a boast, an endorsement or a claim about the coin, or outlets repeating it unchecked; unclear when nothing solid was found.

why.description: One plain sentence, 140 characters at most: what the research found.

sources.description: Up to 4 pages found in this research that back the opinion. Never an invented url.

url.description: The page's full http or https address.

claims.description: One entry per <claim> in <claims>, in the same order. Empty when there are none.

quote.description: The claim's text, copied exactly from its <claim> tag.

opinion.description: likely_true when independent sources support it, likely_false when they contradict it, unclear when nothing solid was found.

why.description: One plain sentence, 140 characters at most: what the research found.

sources.description: Up to 4 pages found in this research that back the opinion. Never an invented url.

url.description: The page's full http or https address.

tech.description: Your rating of the product or technology the coin claims: whether it exists and works as said, and whether anyone would find it useful beyond trading this coin. Price, hype and the coin's market are not part of it.

score.description: 1 to 10 by the prompt's anchors. null when the coin claims no product or technology: a meme, a story or a community is not tech.

why.description: One plain sentence, 140 characters at most: what the research found.

sources.description: Up to 4 pages found in this research that back the score. Never an invented url.

url.description: The page's full http or https address.

summary.description: One plain sentence, 160 characters at most, written after the facts: it opens with the answer the prompt's rule gives for them, then the reason that decides it.

story_link.description: Whether the coin is tied to the story or article it rests on. null when the coin rests on no story.

status.description: tied: someone in the story (the article, the linked post's author, the people or outlet in it) names, backs or made the coin, shown by a source found in this research. named_after: the coin takes its name, ticker, picture or words from the story, but nobody in the story is shown to be tied to it. not_tied: the coin's name, picture and words do not match the story it links.

why.description: One plain sentence, 140 characters at most: what ties the coin to the story, or what is missing.

red_flags.description: Up to 3 short plain phrases a buyer should know, 50 characters at most each, the most serious first. Empty when there are none.
